map.summary: This area turns a parsed document into ordered, ready-to-search pieces. It keeps each piece inside one heading section, packs text up to a token budget with a little overlap, and rebuilds Markdown headings so context is preserved. Each piece gets a stable identifier derived from its document, settings, and content. It runs as a library step; how it is called or where results go next is not shown.
unknowns: No call site invoking chunk_document is shown; wiring from parsing into chunking and from chunks into embedding, indexing, or storage is inferred from the public contract alone (F0001, F0016).
How ParsedDocument and ParsedBlock are produced upstream of this area is not covered by the supplied findings (F0001, F0016).
What downstream consumers do with the emitted pieces, including their identifier and embedding text, is outside the supplied evidence (F0010, F0016).
Which symbols the package __init__ re-exports is not shown (F0016).

diagrams.title: How a parsed document becomes searchable pieces
diagrams.description: A parsed document is split by heading section, packed into token-budgeted pieces with overlap, enriched with reconstructed headings, and given stable identifiers.

diagrams.title: How oversized blocks are split
diagrams.description: Blocks accumulate while they fit the token budget; a block that will not fit is split at the longest fitting prefix, and leftover text carries into the next piece.

diagrams.title: What stops the process
diagrams.description: A piece must always hold its heading plus at least one source token; if that cannot fit the configured budget, chunking stops with an error instead of producing an invalid piece.

diagrams.title: Where stable identifiers come from
diagrams.description: Settings are validated and turned into a version digest; that version, the document identifier, position, and content are hashed together so identical input always yields the same piece identifier.

F0001.statement: chunk_document is the subsystem's entry point: it accepts a document_id, a ParsedDocument, a TextTokenizer, and an optional ChunkingConfig, and returns an ordered tuple of Chunk records. It groups document.blocks by each block's locator.heading_path using groupby, then chunks each section independently so no chunk crosses a heading boundary.

F0002.statement: Chunking is deterministic and structure-aware per the package docstring; the algorithm label is 'structure-aware-v1' (CHUNKING_ALGORITHM) and is stamped into config versioning.

F0003.statement: _chunk_section greedily packs whole ParsedBlock fragments into a candidate while the candidate's token count stays within config.max_tokens, popping blocks from a pending list and tracking whether a whole block was added.

F0004.statement: When a block does not fit (or the current candidate is heading-only), _largest_fitting_prefix performs a binary search over the fragment's token spans to find the longest prefix whose combined candidate stays within max_tokens; the leftover text becomes a new _Fragment remainder on the pending block.

F0005.statement: If even a heading-plus-one-token chunk cannot fit, _chunk_section raises ChunkingError with the message 'Heading context and one source token exceed the chunk token limit', making the token budget a hard failure boundary.

F0006.statement: After emitting a chunk, _trailing_overlap reconstructs trailing content from the candidate by re-tokenizing the joined content text and taking the last config.overlap_tokens tokens, seeding the next candidate's carry when pending blocks remain.

F0007.statement: _candidate enforces that all fragments share one heading_path ('A chunk cannot cross a heading boundary') and joins fragment text with double newlines to form content_text; it passes content_text, heading_path, and any leading heading block to build_embedding_text, then counts tokens on the embedding text for token_count.

F0008.statement: build_embedding_text reconstructs Markdown headings by joining '# '*level + heading for each level in heading_path, and strips a leading heading block from the body if it duplicates the leaf heading so the heading is not embedded twice; it raises ValueError on invalid inputs or mismatched leading heading.

F0009.statement: A Chunk record carries document_id, config_version, order, content_text, embedding_text, embedding_token_count, and source_spans; validation requires nonblank texts, positive order and token count, a nonempty tuple of SourceSpan, and source spans sorted in source order.

F0010.statement: Chunk.chunk_id is computed by stable_digest over document_id, config_version, order, content_text, embedding_text, and each span's canonical_value, producing a prefixed digest ('chk_'); this content-addressed identity is what downstream consumers can use as a stable key.

F0011.statement: SourceSpan captures a half-open character range (start_char, end_char) within one parser block, validated nonnegative start and end greater than start, and canonicalizes to JSON including block_number, page_number, and heading_path from the SourceLocator.

F0012.statement: stable_digest builds a length-prefixed SHA-256 over a versioned namespace ('hybrid-rag-search/<namespace>/v1') followed by each UTF-8 value, yielding collision-resistant deterministic identities reused for document and chunk IDs.

F0013.statement: DocumentContentIdentity derives document_id ('doc_<digest>') from tenant_id, collection_id, and content_sha256, so document identity is scoped to authorization boundaries and original file content; chunks then embed this document_id.

F0014.statement: ChunkingConfig validates that max_tokens is a positive integer, overlap_tokens is nonnegative and strictly less than max_tokens, embedding_limit_tokens is positive and at least max_tokens, and tokenizer/algorithm fields are nonblank with a valid 64-hex SHA-256 tokenizer hash; its version property yields 'chunkcfg_<digest>' over the canonical JSON of these fields.

F0015.statement: The default config uses max_tokens=400, overlap_tokens=50, embedding_limit_tokens=512, and pins the tokenizer to the Cohere embed-english-light-v3 model, revision, and SHA-256, so chunk identity is tied to a specific tokenizer artifact.

F0016.statement: How chunk_document is invoked at runtime, how ParsedDocument/ParsedBlock are produced upstream, and how emitted Chunks are embedded, indexed, or stored downstream are not shown in these excerpts; the wiring from parsing to chunking and from chunks to storage is inferred from the public contract alone.
